definition.text: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

facts.text: The light-dependent reactions produce ATP and NADPH from sunlight.

anchor.quote: The light-dependent reactions capture energy from sunlight to produce ATP and NADPH

facts.text: The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into sugar.

facts.text: Oxygen is released as a byproduct of splitting water molecules.

definition.text: The cell membrane is a selectively permeable barrier that regulates which substances enter and leave the cell.

anchor.quote: a selectively permeable barrier that regulates which substances enter and leave the cell

facts.text: The membrane is composed of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

anchor.quote: composed of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins

facts.text: The membrane maintains the internal environment while allowing exchange of nutrients and wastes.

anchor.quote: maintains the internal environment of the cell while allowing the exchange of nutrients and wastes

misconceptions.text: Students think the membrane is a solid wall rather than a fluid, selectively permeable bilayer.

examples.text: Oxygen diffuses freely across the membrane while large charged ions require protein channels.
